name: e⁺e⁻ → Z H (Higgs-strahlung)
explanation: An electron and positron annihilate into a virtual Z, which radiates a Higgs boson and becomes a real Z. The Higgs couples to the Z with a strength proportional to the Z mass.

name: H → Z Z* → Z μ⁺μ⁻
explanation: The Higgs decays to one real Z and one off-shell Z*, which then splits into a muon pair. The Higgs is lighter than two Z masses, so one of the Z bosons must be virtual.

name: H → γγ (W-boson loop)
explanation: The Higgs has no direct coupling to photons, so it decays to two photons through a loop of charged particles, here a W⁺ triangle. Loops of heavy W bosons and top quarks made this channel central to the 2012 Higgs discovery.

name: H → γγ (top-quark loop)
explanation: A Higgs decays to two photons through a triangle of virtual top quarks, which couple strongly to the Higgs and carry electric charge. This loop interferes destructively with the W loop.

name: g g → H (top-quark loop)
explanation: Gluons carry no mass, so they reach the Higgs only through a loop of virtual quarks, dominated by the heavy top quark. Gluon fusion is the largest Higgs production mode at the LHC.
